case_results.wording: A well-written machine looks like an organic being: its parts are in proportion, and its shape fits what it does. Code that keeps growing in one direction is missing an abstraction: a truck seventy-three meters long is a train not yet seen, which needs its carts linked and a rail to run on, or a fleet of trucks, which needs a coordinator and its drivers; the ground it is to cover decides which.

Whenever the design expands into another part of the system, the designer steps back: where does this part fit, and does its shape fit its intended use? The answer may be that the whole anatomy is redone, because this is a different animal.

An agent that wants a line in the psyche submits it through the regular interface, and a judgment is run on the submission before anything changes. The judgment asks whether the line is already said somewhere in the psyche, the same or nearly; whether it is going into the wrong module; and whether the module it is going into is inadequately named.
The Mind Nexus tracks issues and dependencies, and everything that touches the code and its version control.
A module may hold for every version of its topic, including versions not yet begun: its version field is `all`, and a flow bound to any version of that topic is given it.
Usage is fuel, and fuel is life or death: a machine out of usage stops.
The submitted line defines an ephemeral flow as continuous and taking many jobs. L19 says an ephemeral flow is a single flow with a single job and no continuity.
